note: Tuesday 07:00 SGT sweep, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Mon 20 Jul US close — levels/quotes are as of that close and Monday's Asia session unless noted. Every item source-verified (dates, numbers, attributions checked against the cited pages).

items.headline: Silver ticks up to ~$57 Monday after a violent Middle East weekend, but stays ~50% below its January record
items.summary: COMEX silver rose ~0.7-1.55% Monday to ~$56.8-57.0/oz (Sept futures opened $55.96 and hit ~$57.05 intraday), outperforming gold, which slipped ~0.4% toward $4,000. The bid came from escalating US-Iran fighting even as higher-for-longer Fed fears capped the metal. Silver remains ~50% below its late-January all-time high near $121, so this is a bounce within a deep correction, not a reversal.
items.actionable: The Monday bounce relieves near-term pressure on the levered silver sleeve, but the selloff driver — the oil-led rate-hike repricing — is intact. Treat $55.5-56 as the line to defend; a hawkish surprise into the 28-29 Jul FOMC could break it, so size leverage to survive another 5-10% leg down rather than averaging in.

items.headline: US bombs Iran for a 9th-10th straight night; Hormuz flows down to ~two-thirds of normal, third US soldier killed
items.summary: The US ran a 9th-10th consecutive night of strikes on Iran over the weekend into Monday, with Iran claiming fresh missile salvos and the interim ceasefire effectively dead. Energy Secretary Wright said ~14 mb/d — about two-thirds of pre-conflict traffic — is still moving through the Strait of Hormuz, with some ships rerouting along the Omani coast. President Trump said Iran 'will pay' for the deaths of three US service members, dimming near-term de-escalation hopes.
items.actionable: A firm oil bid supports the energy sleeve, but metals are trading off rates not geopolitics — do not count on gold/silver to hedge the war. The real swing for the whole book is any de-escalation headline, which would deflate the Fed-hike premium crushing silver, gold, semis and HK tech.

items.headline: Brent tops $90 intraday, settles ~$89; Houthis declare maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Brent gained ~1.3% Monday to settle ~$89.2/bbl and WTI ~$82-83, after briefly topping $90 on the Iran escalation before paring on renewed US-Iran diplomatic signals; crude is up ~30% from its July lows. Houthi militants in Yemen declared a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, adding a fresh supply-risk vector on top of Hormuz. US gasoline is near $4/gal, roughly a third above pre-war levels.
items.actionable: Sticky $80s-90s oil is a double edge: bullish for the energy sleeve and the inflation-hedge thesis, but it keeps the Fed higher-for-longer, which is the direct headwind for gold, levered silver and rate-sensitive S-REITs. Watch Iran mediation headlines — they matter more to the book than any single position.

items.headline: Hong Kong tech roars back: Hang Seng +~600pts above 25,000, HS Tech +2.8%; Tencent +3.5%, SMIC +3%+
items.summary: HK stocks rallied hard Monday as Beijing moved to shore up markets: the Hang Seng jumped ~2% back above 25,000, the Hang Seng Tech Index +2.79% and HSCEI +3.01%. Tencent (0700) rose ~3.5%, Xiaomi (1810) and Alibaba +3%+, and foundries SMIC (0981) and Hua Hong +3%+ — China chips trading on domestic AI demand, decoupled from the prior week's US SOX rout. The CSRC convened market participants and two state-backed funds disclosed fresh equity purchases.
items.actionable: Direct tailwind for the Tencent/HK-China tech book — the 'national team' put is back under the market, making China tech one of the few risk pockets with explicit policy support this week. The swing factor now is fiscal follow-through at the late-July Politburo, not PBoC rate cuts.

items.headline: Fed-hike repricing hardens: a September HIKE is now the base case, July 28-29 seen ~63% hold
items.summary: The oil surge has flipped rate expectations hawkish. CME FedWatch now prices the 28-29 Jul FOMC at ~63% hold / ~37% for a 25bp hike, and September at ~28% hold, ~51% for +25bp and ~20% for +50bp — i.e. a hike is the base case by September, with cuts off the table. New Chair Kevin Warsh, whose Senate testimony was well received, reiterated 'prices are too high' and rejected tolerating inflation above 2%; the June SEP pencils PCE at 3.6% for 2026.
items.actionable: This is the dominant macro headwind for the book's highest-beta pain point (levered silver + gold miners) and for SG REITs. The one silver lining: the big cash pile keeps earning ~3.6-4% at the fed-funds floor with optionality — it is dry powder for the metals/rare-earth pullbacks, not dead weight.

items.headline: Gold holds near $4,000 (~$4,005, -0.4%) as the rates channel overwhelms the war bid
items.summary: Gold traded ~$4,001-4,009/oz Monday (-0.4%), consolidating right on the $4,000 shelf near nine-month lows. Safe-haven demand from the active US-Iran war is being capped by a firm dollar (DXY ~100.7) and September hike odds climbing above 50% as oil reignites inflation fears. Gold failing to catch a bid during a shooting war underscores that the metal is trading on real rates, not geopolitics.
items.actionable: $4,000 is the psychological floor for the gold and gold-miner sleeve; GDX has already pulled back ~12% YTD toward ~$71-72 support. A decisive break of $4,000 would pressure the leveraged miners further — watch that line into the FOMC.

items.headline: PBoC holds Loan Prime Rates steady for a 14th straight month (1-yr 3.00%, 5-yr 3.50%)
items.summary: At Monday's monthly fixing the People's Bank of China left the one-year LPR at 3.00% and the five-year at 3.50%, unchanged for a 14th consecutive month, despite Q2 GDP slowing to a soft 4.3% y/y (weakest since Q4 2022). Beijing continues to favor liquidity provision over aggressive cuts, keeping the burden on fiscal delivery. HK equities rallied anyway on state-fund support.
items.actionable: No fresh easing tailwind for China/HK exposure today — the market ignored it and rose on the 'national team' bid. The next real catalyst is the late-July Politburo meeting; look for concrete bond-issuance acceleration (RMB6.8tn quota still unused) rather than softer language before sizing up China risk.

items.headline: China tightens rare-earth/magnet export enforcement as US buildout accelerates; MP rides DoD deal, Lynas +63% in 3 months
items.summary: MOFCOM Announcement No. 26 (effective 1 July) formalized a public reporting mechanism for strategic-mineral export-control violations, and on 16-17 July the China Rare Earth Industry Association toured Dongguan magnet makers — signaling continued tight coordination after China added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export-control list on 22 June. On the ex-China side, MP's DoD 'second magnet plant' deal (toward ~10,000t US capacity, Pentagon ~15% stake) underpins the stock, and Lynas has surged ~63% over three months amid its 1 July CEO handover to Pol Le Roux.
items.actionable: The rare-earth watchlist thesis (China curbs + Western onshoring) is validated on both sides. Lynas is the relative winner (not on China's list) and reports June-quarter results Wednesday 22 Jul; MP fights a China entity-list overhang despite ~$82-85 sell-side targets. Treat this basket as event-driven and chop-prone.

items.headline: Semis recover ~1.9% Monday after a brutal week; megacap tech earnings loom
items.summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose ~1.9% Monday, clawing back part of the prior week's sharp selloff (SOX -11% on the month, triggered partly by weak Samsung results and TSMC capex guidance). The S&P 500 was roughly flat-to-slightly-lower and the Nasdaq near flat as investors positioned ahead of major tech earnings later in the week. Chip sentiment feeds directly into SMIC and HK-tech beta.
items.actionable: The chip bounce is a relief for HK-tech read-through (SMIC), but it is a dead-cat until megacap earnings confirm the AI-capex story. The book's US-semis exposure remains the market's soft spot; watch whether the recovery holds through this week's reports before assuming the SOX washout is done.

items.headline: Three S-REITs — Keppel DC REIT, Suntec, Mapletree Industrial — report Thursday 23 July
items.summary: The first real test of the S-REIT sleeve this season lands Thursday. Keppel DC REIT is the strongest set-up: last DPU S$0.02833 (+13.2% YoY), distributable income +20.7% to S$74.6m, leverage 35.1% and ~51% rental reversion on renewals. Suntec's last DPU was S$0.01936 (+23.9% YoY) on thin NPI growth; Mapletree Industrial Trust is the laggard with full-year DPU S$0.1271 (-6.3% YoY) and leverage rising toward ~37.5%.
items.actionable: Expect dispersion, not a sector move — Keppel DC's data-centre momentum is the bull case, MIT's shrinking DPU the warning. Check which of the three you actually hold before Thursday; higher-for-longer rates from the oil shock are a headwind for the whole S-REIT complex.

items.headline: Bitcoin soft over the weekend, ~$64.5k Monday; crypto Fear & Greed at 29 (Fear)
items.summary: Bitcoin opened Monday ~$64,680 and traded around $64,200-64,600 (-0.2% on 24h), holding the $64k shelf through the weekend war headlines but sitting far below the Oct-2025 ATH (~$126k). ETH modestly outperformed BTC on the day; SOL coiled in a tight range under 'extreme fear'. The crypto Fear & Greed Index sits at 29 ('Fear'), up one point from the prior day.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but BTC's relative-strength through the metals/semis selloff makes it a useful risk barometer for HK tech. A break of the ~$62,450 support area would be the risk-off tell if war/Fed news worsens.

items.headline: Uranium holds ~$86/lb; miners still weak despite structural deficit and hyperscaler nuclear deals
items.summary: Spot U3O8 was ~$85.7/lb as of 19 July, consolidating in an $84-87 band after January's spike above $101. Miners and ETFs (CCJ, UUUU ~$13.8, URA ~$43.2) remain in near-term downtrends even as hyperscaler nuclear procurement (Meta, Amazon, Microsoft) and a widening supply-demand gap support the long-term bull case. Energy Fuels' $725M Pentagon loan remains the sector's marquee US-policy catalyst.
items.actionable: Weak tape, strong fundamentals — the uranium slice of the watchlist is catalyst-light near term and hostage to broad risk appetite. UUUU's dual uranium+rare-earth policy support is the multi-quarter call; don't expect it to lead until risk-on returns.

items.headline: Singapore small/mid-caps trounced the STI in 1H 2026; blue-chip + high-yield REIT rotation in focus
items.summary: SGX-listed stocks broadly delivered roughly twice the STI's return in 1H 2026, with attention on names outperforming the index and industrial REITs yielding above 6%. Commentary emphasizes pairing blue chips (DBS — which crossed S$200B market cap on 13 Jul, the first SGX company ever — and Singtel, which launched a S$2B buyback on 9 Jul) with high-yield REITs for resilient income into a higher-for-longer backdrop. The STI itself is consolidating just below its ~5,561 record.
items.actionable: Constructive backdrop for the SGX bank/REIT sleeve: DBS and Singtel are returning capital aggressively (buybacks), a support under the blue-chip book. The pullback from records is consolidation on war/tech jitters, not a bank-specific problem — no action needed unless the STI breaks the ~5,400 area.
